original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design and test an engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR2.TargetedImprovements:Enabling direct sampling of all 5G frequency bands, providing an RF front end and Digital Signal Processing chip to achieve flexible 5G NTN communication with 20%reduction in power consumption compared to the current state of the art.Description: Current RF Systems-on-Chip (SoC) enables direct sampling in Frequency Range 1 (FR1), but higher frequency ranges still require down-conversion stages to sample atbaseband. There is a significant market need for a solution that enables direct sampling across all 5G frequency bands, simplifying the system architecture and improving theefficiency of5G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN). As payload capacity and re-configuration requirements increase, the conventional functions - such as separate analoguereceiver / transmitter, filtering and DSP - become more complex, power hungry and with a time to market which is not suitable for a fast-moving NTN scenario. To address thesechallenges, direct RF sampling with wide bandwidth and software-defined architecture offer a simple, scalable, and efficient solution. It supports flexible frequency planning,reduces filtering requirements and enables higher modulation schemes for higher throughput. In addition, integrated DSP enables agile frequency tuning, on-chip digital signalprocessing, and clock for multichip synchronization. Integrated digital signal processing will support the transition to software-defined radio payloads, creating a highlyconfigurable, common hardware / software device that can be used in next generation of communication satellites.This activity will identify discrete Commercial-of-The-Shelf (COTS) ADC / DAC or mixed-signal chips capable of direct sampling of Frequency Range 2 (FR 2), covering both KuandKa-Band. An engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR will be designed and manufactured. Testing shallevaluate the full Radio Unit (RU) functionality - including RF and lower / upper parts of the physical layer (Low-PHY / High-PHY) .Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. original.description: The Copernicus Sentinel-2 Next Generation space component, which is the subject of this procurement, will ensure a seamless continuation of the current Sentinel-2 first generation capabilities, whilst increasing both the quantity and quality of the products. The development of the Sentinel-2 Next Generation (Sentinel-2 NG) Space Component aims to build upon and enhance the initial observations provided by the first generation. In particular, Sentinel-2 NG (S2NG) will respond to the needs of Copernicus Services, with particular emphasis to the Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and the Emergency Management Service (CEMS), together with, as secondary objective, the Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties,  together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include:  - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at: - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_business - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/How_to_do/esa-star_Registration_Process Please note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Full" registration.

original.description: Objective: To develop innovative end-to-end payload system architectures, techniques and algorithms enabling large distributed arrays for PNT based on high-gain beamforming.Description: Large arrays of antennas and distributed arrays of antennas are being considered for the generation of very high-gain beamforming. In this case, the main objective is to achieve a high received power by the ground user receivers, such that high data rates can be supported per user. Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Implementation of the required tools/software enabling the assessment of the proposed techniques and algorithms; - Assessment/test of the different techniques and algorithms in simulated conditions; - Identification of themost promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained; - Definition of the proposed the way-forward to further matureeach of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
